# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark — agent entry point

Thesis: this repo is a RECORD OF RESULTS and their reproduction path, not a fleet diary.
Serve it, benchmark it, extend it — everything below is public-artifact reproducible.

Results (full tables + row IDs in `data/results.jsonl`):
- default profile (stock `eugr/spark-vllm-b12x:nightly-20260925`, KV block32, b12x
  spec-config backends): cold prefill 8K 3,558 / 16K 3,575 / 128K 2,841 tok/s (steady,
  two full repeats; an intermittent high tuning cluster 4,4–4,7xx is unattributed — quote
  the steady cluster); C1 cold decode 63.3–64.3 tok/s (steps/s 36.1); C8 249.2;
  5.49M-token FP8-KV pool at TP4.
- decode-max profile (`tp4/overlay.decode-max.yml`, public wheel rebuild): steps/s 37.0
  measured pre-promotion state; default is 36.1 current-state — ranking PENDING a
  same-state rerun (tuning-state shifts are proven on this stack).
- vs the Fujitsu sparkring r37 reference (same model/hardware): prefill parity +0…5%,
  C1 cold decode +18…+20%, C8 big lead vs their cold wall / parity vs their warm wall;
  realistic-prompt C1 58.3 current-config — BELOW author warm wall -29%, regime split in flight;
  The famous "author gap" was a warm-window-vs-cold-wall metric artifact — see
  `SPARKRING.md` before repeating it.

Read order:
1. `README.md` — results tables, hardware prerequisites, reproduce-it commands, invariants,
   quality honesty box.
2. `tp4/compose.yml` + `tp4/serve.sh` + `tp4/*.env` (same set in `tp2/`) — the config that
   produced every number. No overlay needed for the default.
3. `SPARKRING.md` — reference-stack scoreboard + the b12x pairing law: which b12x wheels
   even start against which vLLM (stale mainline FAILS startup; fresh main runs but
   regresses prefill) + env-lever keep/retire table (block32 and spec-backends keep;
   async-off / dispatch / CROSS_NIC flat).
4. `data/results.jsonl` — every number incl. `author-r37-*` reference rows;
   `data/README.md` — instrument semantics (wall vs decode-window; steps/s normalization).
5. `tools/ldb-fast-matrix.sh` (bench cycle), `tools/smoke.sh` (behavior gate),
   `tools/bench-quick.py` (realistic-prompt probe); `tp4/README.md` pitfalls before
   touching a live multi-rank fleet.

Hard invariants (violating any produces a broken or dishonest deployment):
- All ranks run the SAME image ID (check `docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}'`, not tags).
- Start workers → coordinator; stop coordinator → workers.
- `NCCL_IB_MERGE_NICS=0`, `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3`, HC TP-shard ONLY at TP4 (`HC_TP=0` at TP2).
- Per-image-profile cache namespaces (vllm/triton/flashinfer/b12x); never share.
- Keep MemAvailable >= 16 GiB on the limiting rank; the KV budget is a safety setting.
- Smoke before benching; re-run any suspiciously slow first arm (acceptance and one-off
  autotune stalls move single cells; steps/s + accept are recorded per row — read both).
- FP8 KV has a documented quality caveat (root README honesty box); BF16-KV rows exist.
- Weights: use the QAD revision `629bc3218833a38b475b719f34aa571666f4a03e` — the model
  repo's `main` is NOT a substitute (author's own warning; we verified byte-identity).
